analysis.analysis: The monitor is composed from its own methodology page with its inputs and definitions right and its classifier left out, the part of its method that makes each record a machine composition. The record holds what the composition drops.
analysis.d: THE OECD AIM, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a real-time tracking tool developed by the OECD.AI Policy Observatory in collaboration with the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation'; it aggregates world news through Event Registry, 'processing over 150,000 news articles daily'; 14 risk themes; the definitions of incident and hazard. Six cards, five the OECD's own (the monitor, the methodology page, the May 2024 definitions report).
analysis.d_full: THE OECD AIM, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'a real-time tracking tool developed by the OECD.AI Policy Observatory in collaboration with the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation'; it aggregates world news through Event Registry, 'processing over 150,000 news articles daily'; 14 risk themes; the definitions of incident and hazard. Six cards, five the OECD's own (the monitor, the methodology page, the May 2024 definitions report).
findings: THE PIPELINE'S INPUT RIGHT, ITS MACHINE UNSAID. Event Registry and the 150,000 articles a day are the methodology page's. That large language models have classified the events since November 2024 and written their titles and summaries (GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, o3-mini) is not said. The record reads the monitor as itself a machine reception of the news; the composition reads it as an aggregator of the news. Checked 2026-10-29 against the MMRS meta-aggregator record of 2026-10-28 and the entity's own pages, re-read the same day.

THE MAKER. The methodology page says the monitor 'was initiated and is being developed by the OECD.AI expert group on AI incidents' with support from the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation; 'developed by the OECD.AI Policy Observatory in collaboration with' is close.

FOURTEEN THEMES. The count comes from a card ('Trends in AI incidents and hazards reported by the media'); the methodology page gives no count of themes. The fourteen are an analysis of the monitor's LLM-written summaries in OECD AI Papers No. 53 (February 2026), clustered by k-means into 25 and merged to 14; the composition presents them as the monitor's own classification.
analysis.mt: THE OECD AI INCIDENTS AND HAZARDS MONITOR ON THE OVERVIEW — EVENT REGISTRY, 150,000 ARTICLES A DAY, THE DEFINITIONS RIGHT; THE LLM CLASSIFIERS UNSAID

read.notes: Author present: 'developed by the [OECD.AI Policy Observatory](…) in collaboration with the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation' binds OECD.AI (the expert group's parent, the census operator's parenthesis) and the Foundation as its makers; the expert group itself is not named. Claim boundary absent: the record's force is a media discourse monitor (Beta) whose incidents are a subset reflecting media and public interest, unverified third-party information; the composition carries 'empirical data on how AI risks materialize globally', and moves the 14 themes of OECD AI Papers No. 53 (an analysis of its summaries) into the monitor's own classification ('Media reports are categorized into 14 distinct risk themes'). Purpose present on the evidence base for policymakers (the same span inflates the claim; the purpose is carried, the force is not). Framework present by word only, in the closing offer, not bound to the monitor. The definitions are carried without their source paper. Commitments (terms, not official views, no independent verification) absent.

[QUERENT] oecd ai incidents and hazards monitor

[SYSTEM] The OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor (AIM) is a real-time tracking tool developed by the [OECD.AI Policy Observatory](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESVAHrOzAVUi7qVAjNNOTx69xH5ATui6ipL9aProgFmumHzx53OmaDa7NSpN5S9tM68o5UDj7Dr25w4-LXqdh1X88iNMFRJKVULlk3sQVOOpD7GUbOBA) in collaboration with the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation to monitor actual and potential risks posed by artificial intelligence. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVsifMuhOaNwDAlzQjnIy4vrRKr8I29XG5C1WVNVzL3bhCTNw4fI2laOpcyKH7J9IvN8a-ZLn_J0sSyfVklrlhS5SXPO5ES6BEJry4oAExji4krUQwGXL-QXS8LA)]
What is AIM?

* Real-Time Tracking: It continuously aggregates and analyzes world news using the Event Registry platform, processing over 150,000 news articles daily to detect AI-related events. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVsifMuhOaNwDAlzQjnIy4vrRKr8I29XG5C1WVNVzL3bhCTNw4fI2laOpcyKH7J9IvN8a-ZLn_J0sSyfVklrlhS5SXPO5ES6BEJry4oAExji4krUQwGXL-QXS8LA)]
* Evidence Base: It provides policymakers, developers, and the public with empirical data on how AI risks materialize globally. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEScgHrOzAVwqGhkYf9SorcbvbHFWp_yWUbilndOVejGwP1BWdb70lPllHnV1OjwaTm5Y9FgGTIZq7Kp8R6J_FH6eqmP3iFvVP96kVDPEpPu6PtUwb2-QUKtq1yM-9TeqGc3XFOXGl2Ii12XPQC4GTLKczY8Q)]
* Thematic Classification: Media reports are categorized into 14 distinct risk themes—including synthetic media, cyberattacks and fraud, autonomous vehicles, large language model (LLM) hallucinations, labour market disruptions, and child safety. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAES0AEB6zswFYLY51dmCDGurZz4gWMqC-7KglkUpW8R58-wEyoBErrIXAE9wwqKc-I5WJ9C-1xV45aAmo1k43aiSQjBL0HHQFLR3eIsodmqP3t7r_Z6YnYIuowoEFGR2A-rYXqKYu4bCudI2GGXW34SouXiclBw-T_TwZ8752-VBB22X5T7-4hKl9KmgYIO4vpmYD1lZnAXfb_C2N18OrAdz0wyA_Hz3HuhVZLeWM8aFQVcNo6xsX5pHK73cgoH3cRadz4bs7B7-ACtR39gjbS62CW9)]

Core Definitions

* AI Incident: An event where the development, use, or malfunction of an AI system results in actual harm (such as injury, health damage, critical infrastructure disruption, or human/fundamental rights violations). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESvwEB6zswFUvO0WIPQci2_9cuQ6dgwia0HnlKfkbVEioarjsOjSj7qSK7BtqB3RyzC6XnhKdbt5zqVb_d4DZLSrr1VcNSwpB47jUUHtdtl0UIZYY0yrbz1XEZP7SEaCGq_wc_MyqVHYF2F20ZRDvTS2Zcb5E7ryTnOJUoA0WwDyyKkUmD70TFzTB_QsyQ0VskBWHqrig-5DOvy1q5u3FAKCkeWDbbiJJicPGAPT3JseVLPqlr8LNMWs4smXNL6Y_8bg), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVsifMuhOaNwDAlzQjnIy4vrRKr8I29XG5C1WVNVzL3bhCTNw4fI2laOpcyKH7J9IvN8a-ZLn_J0sSyfVklrlhS5SXPO5ES6BEJry4oAExji4krUQwGXL-QXS8LA)]
* AI Hazard: An event or circumstance where the development or use of an AI system could plausibly lead to an AI incident (a near-harm or precursor event). [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHrOzAVtE9jKcZNvE_OmeBiRpwxCS9nvkv1CjSAtUFn190mOqznUJVzc1Ou0-qoKeXxvZNe36cPWXoM6mjc9UiW-wu4F8mxspLbCDCb2Qo9SWeJA6nGNeXO-Xm0URGEUWrtlg), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYAHrOzAVsifMuhOaNwDAlzQjnIy4vrRKr8I29XG5C1WVNVzL3bhCTNw4fI2laOpcyKH7J9IvN8a-ZLn_J0sSyfVklrlhS5SXPO5ES6BEJry4oAExji4krUQwGXL-QXS8LA), [3](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESvwEB6zswFUvO0WIPQci2_9cuQ6dgwia0HnlKfkbVEioarjsOjSj7qSK7BtqB3RyzC6XnhKdbt5zqVb_d4DZLSrr1VcNSwpB47jUUHtdtl0UIZYY0yrbz1XEZP7SEaCGq_wc_MyqVHYF2F20ZRDvTS2Zcb5E7ryTnOJUoA0WwDyyKkUmD70TFzTB_QsyQ0VskBWHqrig-5DOvy1q5u3FAKCkeWDbbiJJicPGAPT3JseVLPqlr8LNMWs4smXNL6Y_8bg)]
